Q: How do I check when my raycast exists the collision shape for a specific value to be switched to "false"? A:

The suggested early return does the same thing you’re already doing, only with slightly nicer code (less nesting).

Your issue seems to be that you never hide the interaction UI. Because you’re using interaction_raycast.get_collider() to find the door each frame, you can’t call view_door_label(false) when it is no longer hit, because when it isn’t hit, you have no reference to it. So you can:

Keep a reference to the currently viewed door

Then you can hide the label in the raycast code:

var current_door: PhysicsBody3D = null

func item_interaction():
    if !interaction_raycast.is_colliding():
        if current_door:
            current_door.view_door_label(false)
            current_door = null
        return
        
    var raycast_collider = interaction_raycast.get_collider()
    if raycast_collider.is_in_group("openable_closeable_door"):
        current_door = raycast_collider
        current_door.view_door_label(true)
Let the door handle it

Since the door owns its own label in your setup, I would prefer this one. This also shifts the responsibility from the player better. The player is not responsible for actually displaying or hiding the label, they just inform the door that they’re looking at it right now. And when they no longer view it, they just stop telling it. This would be the door’s code:

var is_viewed: bool = false
var was_viewed_last_frame: bool = false

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
    if is_viewed:
        #obvious
        door_label.visible = true
    elif was_viewed_last_frame:
        #we’re currently not viewed, but we were viewed
        #last frame – player just stopped looking at us
        door_label.visible = false
        
    #update values for next frame
    was_viewed_last_frame = is_viewed
    is_viewed = false

func view_door_label() -> void:
    is_viewed = true
Use a timer

You could also use a timer to hide the label after a short interval and keep resetting it every frame the player looks at the door.

Unrelated concerns

By the way, I would probably advise against using groups for this. You probably have more things that should react to coming into the raycast, so at the very least I would make a more generic group like “viewables”. But really, given Godot’s lack of interfaces, an idiomatic approach would be to check for a method name:

func item_interaction():
    if !interaction_raycast.is_colliding():
        return
        
    var collider = interaction_raycast.get_collider()

    if collider.has_method(&"handle_interaction_interest"):
        collider.handle_interaction_interest()

    if Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"interact") and collider.has_method(&"handle_interaction"):
        collider.handle_interaction()

    if Input.is_action_pressed(&"interact") and collider.has_method(&"handle_continuous_interaction"):
        collider.handle_continuous_interaction()

No more mention of doors at all. The player class doesn’t need to know whether it’s a door or a chest or a lightswitch, only what interactions are available.

Also, instead of chained get_parent() calls, you may want to use the owner property, but it depends on your scene setup.

Q: Linux shell get value of a field from a yml file A:

You can also use a one-liner with just awk, i.e.:

$ awk '/^[\t ]*test:$/ {found=1} ; /^[\t ]*database:/ {if ( found == 1) {print $2}}' database.yml

Q: .NET 4.5, how to change zone security settings via .NET Framework configuration A:

From MSDN:

On 32-bit computers, create a subkey under the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft.NETFramework key in the system registry. Use the key name LegacyMyComputerZone with a DWORD value of 1.

On 64-bit computers, create a subkey under the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft.NETFramework key in the system registry. Use the key name LegacyMyComputerZone with a DWORD value of 1. Create the same subkey under the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Microsoft.NETFramework key.

Q: Windows Active Directory monitoring with zabbix A:

You should look into "Zabbix Integrations", here you can find a ready template with these checks:

Check windows event log: * Create user account * User account on * User account off * User account password reset * Delete user account * Unlocked user account + changed domain policy and cleaned security log

You can extend it with your own checks (i.e.: powershell scripts).
